Instead of crashing, my mood just swings between feeling on top of the world and getting extremely irritable and snapping at my wife or my crew when I feel like they're slowing down my plans.\n\nDoctor: Have you engaged in any impulsive behaviors, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or impulsive decisions, during these periods of high energy and feeling 'on top of the world'?\n\nPatient: Yes, I've made some really impulsive financial decisions. I bought a bunch of expensive tools and solar inventory on credit for a business that doesn't even exist yet, which has run up major debts and made my wife furious. At the time, I felt so confident in my big plans that it seemed completely justified to me.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any distractibility or difficulty focusing on one task for an extended period, or do you find you can hyper-focus on your projects despite the constant stream of new ideas?\n\nPatient: I'm definitely extremely distractible rather than hyper-focused. When I try to focus on wiring or studying, every little thing like a buzzing phone, a humming light, or a new idea completely pulls my attention away. I end up dropping tasks halfway through to start something else, leaving behind a mess of unfinished projects.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep, due to your racing thoughts or high energy levels?\n\nPatient: Yes, my sleep has dropped dramatically—most nights I only lie down for two or three hours because my mind is constantly racing with wiring diagrams and business plans. I don't even feel tired, just completely wired and ready to keep working. Honestly, sleeping feels like a total waste of time when I have so much to get done.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if you've experienced these symptoms of high energy, distractibility, and impulsive decisions consistently throughout your life, or if this is a relatively new development for you?\n\nPatient: No, this isn't a lifelong thing at all; it's a relatively new development for me. This intense overdrive has been building and staying constant for about the last seven months, ever since I took on a big commercial solar contract and started studying nights for my Master Electrician exam.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned this intense overdrive has been constant for about seven months, but can you tell me if there was a specific event or period that triggered this change, or if it seemed to come on gradually over time?\n\nPatient: It definitely came on gradually, building up over the last seven months. It's just felt like a continuous, steady build-up of intense energy over the whole seven months without any real breaks. At home, my wife is furious about the massive credit card debts I ran up buying tools and solar inventory, and she says I'm never present anymore since I stopped going to family barbecues and softball just to work on my projects.\n\nDoctor: You mentioned that this intense overdrive started around the time you took on a massive double workload with studying for your Master Electrician exam and working on a big commercial solar contract. Do you think that if you were to complete these projects or significantly reduce your workload, your symptoms of high energy, distractibility, and impulsive decisions would decrease or resolve?\n\nPatient: I don't really see these behaviors as \"symptoms\" that need to be resolved or fixed. My wife and my boss just don't understand how big this is going to be yet.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning as a result of your high energy and impulsive behaviors, or do you primarily see these traits as beneficial to your goals and aspirations?\n\nPatient: Even though everything is currently in chaos—my boss pulled me off field work because clients complained and the crew felt unsafe, and my wife is furious about the debts and me missing family events—I still feel like this drive is necessary. I honestly believe I'm meant to revolutionize the local solar industry with my ideas, and I've felt like they will all end up thanking me once they see how big this business actually becomes.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where your high energy and impulsive behaviors led to marked impairment in social or occupational functioning, or were they generally seen as goal-oriented and productive, despite causing chaos?\n\nPatient: While I initially felt highly productive and driven, it has definitely crossed the line into causing serious impairment. At work, my boss pulled me off field work because clients complained and my crew felt unsafe with my fast timelines, and at home, my wife is furious about the debts I ran up and the fact that I've stopped attending family barbecues and am never present."

I honestly believe I'm meant to revolutionize the local solar industry with my ideas, and I've felt like they will all end up thanking me once they see how big this business actually becomes.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where your high energy and impulsive behaviors led to marked impairment in social or occupational functioning, or were they generally seen as goal-oriented and productive, despite causing chaos?\n\nPatient: While I initially felt highly productive and driven, it has definitely crossed the line into causing serious impairment. At work, my boss pulled me off field work because clients complained and my crew felt unsafe with my fast timelines, and at home, my wife is furious about the debts I ran up and the fact that I've stopped attending family barbecues and am never present.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any situations or periods where your high energy and driven state did not lead to impairment in your relationships or work, but instead was seen as beneficial or productive by those around you?\n\nPatient: Yes, at the very beginning of this seven-month stretch, my family actually appreciated my extra drive and the long hours I spent in the garage planning a future family-run business.
